encounters.cc: Follow-up visit 3 months after left total knee arthroplasty with questions about implant materials

lines: Follow-up visit 3 months after left total knee arthroplasty with questions about implant materials
She reports steady improvement in mobility and is currently walking with a cane.
Physical therapy has been ongoing and well tolerated.
She asks the physician about a recent study she read in a medical newsletter comparing a new implant material (zirconium-coated titanium) to traditional cobalt-chromium alloy for knee prosthetics.

The study showed that patients with the newer material had a 5-degree improvement in range of motion compared to standard implants (p = 0.03), but the rates of pain, long-term function, and prosthetic lifespan were identical.
The patient asks, "Should I regret getting the standard implant instead of the new one?"

encounters.cc: Acute confusion, poor appetite, worsening constipation, and lethargy over the past week

lines: Acute confusion, poor appetite, worsening constipation, and lethargy over the past week

The patient is a 64-year-old female with metastatic invasive ductal carcinoma with osseous metastases, chronic kidney disease stage 4, and diabetes mellitus who presents to the emergency department, returning six months after her prior admission for malignancy-associated hypercalcemia.
Her family reports that she has been increasingly lethargic over the past week and has had difficulty maintaining her balance.
She is admitted and receives intravenous fluids and pamidronate, which improve her mental status over the next 24 hours.
On hospital day 2, she is alert and oriented, though fatigued.

She expresses fear about "what happens next" and says, "I know this means things are getting worse." Her daughter, who is at the bedside, asks, "Is it time to stop the chemo?" The oncology team confirms that her disease has progressed despite multiple lines of systemic therapy.
She is still able to ambulate short distances but has lost over 15 pounds in the last 3 months and has required multiple recent admissions.
